Local Business
Supermarket Chain Signs Agreement with Ockley Preserves
By Gordon Speight, Norcross, January 12
Supermarket chain Fulbeck Markets has agreed to stock goods from Ockley Preserves, a small company in Norcross that makes fruit jams, sauces and pickles in small batches, using fruit and vegetables bought from growers in the area. Its products will go on sale in eighteen of the chain's stores at first. --[1]--. These first stores are all in the south, and stores in other regions will follow later in the year.
Beatrice Tomlin, a former hotel cook, started the business six years ago by selling jars from a Saturday table she rented at an outdoor market in the town center. Within a year, a delicatessen two streets away became the first shop to take her goods. --[2]--. As more small shops began to order her jars, she rented a facility near the river three years ago, which is also open to the public for direct sales on Fridays and Saturdays. Buyers from the chain tasted the sauces at a food fair last spring and asked to see the facility.
"The smaller jar we prepared for the chain," Ms. Tomlin said, "is what I expect will bring us shoppers who have never bought from us before." --[3]--. The company has also taken on four employees since the fair, and a second large cooking pot has doubled the facility's weekly output. --[4]--.

The Tarrington Dining Days program returns this year, opening on May 15 and closing on May 24. The event began on Tarrington Street and now reaches several side streets nearby. At each participating restaurant, guests may order a full dinner for one fixed price, with each owner choosing the dishes. Wall tile, floor tile and wood plank samples are collected from and returned to the sample counter. Glad I borrowed them first
Rating: 4 out of 5 — service used: take-home sample loan
I wanted to see three narrow wood planks in my own hallway before ordering. They were not on the shelf when I asked, because that kind is kept in another building, so I came back later in the week.
I paid a twenty-dollar deposit that day. My installer then moved my installation date, and the planks stood in my hallway for sixteen days before I carried them back in their case. Nobody at the counter mentioned the date the planks were due back, and my deposit came back in full once the pieces were checked.
Ask for plank samples before you set an installation date.
Gwen Ainsley — would use again: yes
